takeaways: When people set line height to 1.5× the font size, paragraph spacing to 2×, letter spacing to 0.12× and word spacing to 0.16×, no content or function is lost.
You do not have to design with these values. Your layout has to survive people applying them.
Wider spacing makes text longer and taller. Containers that grow with their text survive; fixed boxes clip.
It applies to real text in the page, not text in images. Languages that do not use one of these properties only need the ones they use.
failures: Fixed-height cards that cut off the last line
Button labels that overflow or get truncated
Text that overlaps the element below it
check: Apply a text spacing bookmarklet to the build and use the page.
In your file, make a test version of key components with the four values applied.
Look for clipped, overlapping or truncated text, especially in buttons, tabs and badges.

quiz.question: Brand guidelines set body line height to 1.2. Does that fail 1.4.12?
options: No, as long as the layout survives people raising it
Yes. Line height must be at least 1.5
Yes, unless it is only used for headings
quiz.why: This criterion is about what happens when people override spacing, not about your defaults. Generous spacing still helps readability, but here the test is whether anything breaks.

spec: Mark containers that hold text as hugging their content, not fixed height.
Say how labels behave when they get longer: wrap, grow or scroll, never clip.
Avoid line height and spacing values that rely on text staying exactly one line.
review: Which elements have a fixed height with text inside?
What happens to these tabs if every word gets wider?
Where are we truncating with an ellipsis, and can people still read the full text?
tradeoff: Tight, fixed boxes give a precise look and break first. Let containers grow, and set minimum heights rather than fixed ones, so the design keeps its shape at default and survives at wider spacing.
system: Build text containers with auto layout and minimum heights, and test each component with the four spacing values before release.
pitch: Many people with dyslexia read better with more space between letters and lines. If our layout breaks when they add it, we have locked them out.
